task: Roadmap 4.3 step 6 (plan 8.1-8.2): turn the ATR read from an inference into something a gate holds. Before this, the only evidence the reader worked end to end was a 7-frame difference in gameplay_init between media plus the argument that every failure class diverts away from start_gameplay.
status: PASS - the gate is live and both controls fail it

base.note: refactor(4.3): extract sector_c_drain_clear and export it by name

what_was_added.observer: scripts/atari800-wall-trace.h: DFBootSnapshot gains level_header[8] captured raw and level_checksum over the whole image; three PC-driven counters (command frames at sector_reader_begin_receive, wire retries at sector_reader_settle, the load window from sector_reader_load to the gameplay milestone). The counters ride the reader's own PCs rather than bus traffic - the observer sees one instruction at a time, and a hit at a known label is as good a signal while costing nothing.
what_was_added.gate: scripts/runtime-wall-trace.mjs: at the frame-3300 gameplay snapshot every session's image at LEVEL_BUFFER is compared byte for byte against the build's own build/level-1.bin, XEX sessions must show 0 command frames, ATR sessions exactly one per sector, and no session may need a wire retry - the emulator's wire is lossless, so any retry is a reader defect.

xex_sessions.path: resident skip: the XEX carries the level image as a block (owner decision 1) and never reaches SIO

atr_sessions.path: direct SIO: exactly one command frame per sector at START GAME

level_image.meaning: 'V','S', version 1, level 1, 2 sectors, payload 248 B, reserved 0
level_image.verified: byte-exact against build/level-1.bin on all eight sessions, both media, both cold RAM fills, BASIC enabled and disabled

measured.note: The 7-frame ATR load window is EMULATOR-MEASURED and is a regression signal for the reader's own overhead only. Atari800 spaces bytes at 8 scanlines and models no drive latency, jitter, errors or command-line hold; it is never a hardware figure.

negative_controls.mutation: flip one byte (offset 100) of build/level-1.bin AFTER the artifacts are built, so only the expectation changes
negative_controls.result: FAILED as required: 'xex-a5 has the wrong level image at $a600: header 5653010102f80000 checksum 2410047369, expected ... / 1194891394'
negative_controls.why_it_matters: the header still matched. A header-only check would have passed this. The whole-image checksum is what catches a payload that arrives wrong.

negative_controls.mutation: compare the level magic against LEVEL_MAGIC_0 + 1 in sector_reader_resident_hit, so the skip can never hit
negative_controls.result: FAILED as required: 'xex-a5 did not reach the legal gameplay display/VBI path by frame 3300'
negative_controls.why_it_matters: proves two things at once - that the XEX sessions pass BECAUSE of the resident skip and not because SIO happens to work without a disk, and that a NO_DEVICE really does divert to the failure screen instead of falling through into gameplay.

not_built.claim: Plan 8.3's in-emulator fault injection is NOT implemented. Do not read this file as covering it.
missing: DFTRACE_SIO_CORRUPT_BYTE=n: flip one SERIN byte once, so the reader must succeed with exactly one wire retry. Nothing here exercises the wire-retry path in the emulator; it is covered only by the 6502 harness (tests/sector-reader.test.mjs), where the POKEY stub is scripted.

DFTRACE_SIO_FORCE_ERROR=1: substitute $45 at the C/E position, so the DEVICE_ERROR screen appears and FIRE returns to the menu. The failure SCREEN has never been rendered in any automated run - only its code path is unit-tested.
a stripped-XEX build flag for the NO_DEVICE path. Control B above reaches that state by accident rather than by design, and it asserts nothing about what the player sees.
not_built.consequence: The reader's success path is gated end to end on both media. Its failure paths are gated in the 6502 harness only. The first time a human sees the failure screen will be the owner's SIO2SD smoke.

also_not_observed.animation: The loader-mode animation is drawn (one step per completed sector) but no gate observes it. On a 2-sector level it steps twice, so there is little to see; it becomes worth asserting when 4.6 lands a level large enough for the sweep to be visible.
